Test Method: Potentiodynamic polarization. All studies were carried out with rotating disk electrodes of 0.1 cm2 (diameter 0.357 cm) insulated with a PTFE shrinkable tubing. Experiments were performed at 6000 rpm (in part at 600 rpm) in 1 M HCI at 25°C under a nitrogen atmosphere.
Heat treatment: The binary Fe-Cr alloys were furnished by Climax Molybdenum. They were subsequently hot forged. The other alloys were prepared in our laboratory by alloying to the original Fe-Cr alloys the elements Mo, W, V or Si using a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Microstructures: The metallographic examination revealed the presence of a few oxide inclusions in an otherwise apparently single phase ferritic matrix.
Comments: Pretreatment of the electrodes included grinding with emery papcr and polishing with alumina powder in water to 1/4 μm finish. They were rinsed and cathodically polarized in the working electrolyte at -700 mV(SHE) for 10 min.
